transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I keep losing a lot of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and replaying conversations in my head. Especially before I leave the house or start work—I feel like I have to make sure I didn’t make some serious mistake.
When you find yourself re-reading or replaying things, does it feel driven by an unwanted thought or urge that keeps intruding into your mind?

Yes. It’s like the thought barges in even when I’m trying to focus on work or prepare a lesson—that I sent my ex-wife the wrong message, mishandled family photos, or let somebody in the community down. I know I’ve already gone over it, but I can’t seem to just let it pass.
When you go back to re-read or check, does doing it reduce the anxiety, even if only for a moment?

Yes, for a little while. I’ll re-read the email or open the folder again, and I feel like maybe I’ve checked enough. But it doesn’t last long, and then I start wondering if I missed something, so I go back over it.
Do you feel that all this checking is excessive, even while you’re doing it?

Yes, I do. I know I’ve already read the email or checked the folder, and it seems unreasonable to keep doing it. But before I leave or start work, I get stuck trying to make sure I didn’t make some serious mistake, and I can lose a lot of time going over it again.
When you go back to check, do you feel you have to do it in a particular way or until it feels exactly right?

Yeah. I’ll keep re-reading the email or text, or reopening a folder, until I feel sure I didn’t miss some serious mistake. And if it doesn’t feel settled, I end up replaying the conversation in my head again before I can leave the house or start work.
When you feel compelled to check, is it mainly because you’re afraid that if you don’t, something bad will happen because of a mistake you made?

Yes. I’m afraid I’ve missed something important or made a serious mistake. So I re-read the emails and texts, reopen folders, or replay conversations in my head until I can feel sure. It can take up a lot of time before I can leave the house or get started working.
If you resisted checking, would you feel a strong sense that something bad might happen because of a mistake you missed?

Yes. If I try not to check, I get this strong worry that I’ve overlooked something serious. I can’t really settle until I’ve gone back through the emails or texts, checked the folders, or replayed the conversation again.
Do these checking habits feel unwanted to you, rather than just your preferred way of being careful and thorough?

Yes. I don’t want to spend that much time on it. I lose chunks of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, or replaying conversations before I can leave or start work. It feels like I have to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.
Have you ever felt that this kind of repeated checking is just part of who you are, rather than something unwanted?

No, I don’t see it as just who I am. I came in because I keep losing chunks of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and replaying conversations in my head before I can leave or start work. It feels like I’m trying to prove I didn’t make some serious mistake.
Do you also get repeated intrusive thoughts about having made a serious mistake, even when you are not actively checking?

Yes. Even when I’m trying to focus on a system design or prepare a lesson, the thought barges in that maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, mishandled family photos, or let somebody in the community down. I know I’ve already gone over it, but I can’t just let the thought pass.
